title: Widest Pair of Indices With Equal Range Sum
statement: You are given two 0-indexed arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of the same length `n`, each holding only `0`s and `1`s. Look for index pairs `(i, j)` with `i <= j` for which the elements of `nums1` from `i` through `j` (inclusive) add up to the same value as the elements of `nums2` from `i` through `j`. The width of such a pair is `j - i + 1`. Return the largest width over all valid pairs, or `0` if no pair is valid.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair `(i, j)` with running sums is O(n²). Instead, rewrite the condition: the two range sums are equal exactly when the range sum of `nums1[k] - nums2[k]` is zero. With a running prefix `balance` of those differences, a range from `i` to `j` qualifies when the balance after `j` equals the balance just before `i`. To make the range as wide as possible, pair each `j` with the **earliest** position where the same balance appeared.

## Approach

1. Record that balance `0` is seen at position `-1` (before any element), so ranges starting at index 0 are covered.
2. For each `j`, add `nums1[j] - nums2[j]` to `balance`.
3. If `balance` was seen before at position `p`, the range `p + 1 .. j` has equal sums; its width `j - p` may update `widest`.
4. Otherwise store `j` as the first position of this balance (never overwrite an earlier one).
5. Return `widest` (still `0` if no range qualified).

## Example 1, step by step

`nums1 = [1, 1, 0, 1]`, `nums2 = [0, 1, 1, 0]`. The differences are `1, 0, -1, 1`.
- `j = 0`: `balance = 1`, new, stored at 0.
- `j = 1`: `balance = 1`, first seen at 0, width `1 - 0 = 1`.
- `j = 2`: `balance = 0`, first seen at -1, width `2 - (-1) = 3`.
- `j = 3`: `balance = 1`, first seen at 0, width `3`.

The answer is `3` (for example `i = 1, j = 3`).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time map operations.
- Space: O(n) for `firstSeen` (at most `2n + 1` different balances).

## Pitfalls

- Seed the map with balance `0` at `-1`, or ranges starting at index 0 are missed.
- Keep only the first position of each balance; overwriting it shrinks the widths.
- The width of the range `p + 1 .. j` is `j - p`, not `j - p + 1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `firstSeen` | balance value → earliest position where it occurred |
| `balance` | sum of `nums1[k] - nums2[k]` for `k` up to `j` |
| `widest` | widest valid range found so far |
| `j` | right end of the current range |
